mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, with p-value > 0.10 in a one-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 YoY change and 60-day returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes Fed tightening and higher input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes, or the trigger fails to precede a Fed rate hike in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% in the same month signals a dual monetary-inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the joint trigger occurs in fewer than 5 instances in a 10-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly lower during co-decline episodes (p > 0.10), or the interaction occurs in fewer than 8 months in a 15-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deepening labor market slack, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly different from baseline during these episodes (p > 0.10), or the trigger is not followed by a recession in at least 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of at least 3% following two months of contraction (RSAFS monthly change < -1%) signals a V-shaped demand rebound, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 3% after two consecutive months of RSAFS monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly higher during these rebounds (p > 0.10), or the pattern fails to occur in at least 5 instances over a 10-year period.
